overall: The set reads very much like real TOEIC Part 5 grammar items: each is one workplace or business sentence of natural length, tests one clear point, and draws its distractors from forms of the same word or from same-category connectors, prepositions and tenses. Every item has exactly one defensible answer, and I found no British-versus-American or informal-usage loopholes. The only mild weakness is that a few tense items rely on a single very obvious time marker (e.g. 'two weeks ago', 'at the moment'), which puts them on the easy end of the TOEIC range. The set could use one or two harder items, such as a present perfect versus simple past contrast without an explicit time marker. None of the sentences struck me as copies of published ETS items.
